subject: Future Tech
title: Graphene: The Wonder Sheet
description: A quick win: understand Graphene: The Wonder Sheet.

hook.text: Graphene is a single layer of carbon atoms arranged in a honeycomb. It's the thinnest material possible— one atom thick.

buildup.text: In 2004, two scientists isolated graphene using Scotch tape on graphite. They won the Nobel Prize for peeling tape.

discovery.text: Graphene is 200x stronger than steel, conducts electricity 1,000x better than silicon, and is nearly transparent.

twist.text: Two decades after discovery, graphene hasn't yet revolutionized anything.

climax.text: Graphene is finding niche uses: water filters, battery additives, flexible sensors.

punchline.text: The thinnest material with the biggest promise. Still waiting.
